entities.summary: Leopold Charles Maurice Stennett Amery, also known as L. S. Amery, was a British Conservative Party politician and journalist. During his career, he was known for his interest in military preparedness, British India and the British Empire and for his opposition to appeasement. He was Secretary of State for the Colonies (1924–29), opposed the National Government of the 1930s and served as Secretary of State for India during the Second World War (1940–45). He was also a prolific writer whose output included a multi-volume history of the Second Boer War and several volumes of memoirs and diaries.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Secretary of State for India during World War II, Amery played a key role in shaping British policy towards India and its colonies. His efforts contributed to the eventual decision to grant independence to India in 1947.
